title: Giving the Knowledge Model Governed Structure
description: 2026-04-12. I am working on entity relationships, enterprise types, temporal validity, an APQC tree, local classification, unified search routing, and chunk-level semantic search.
body:
2026-04-12. I am working on entity relationships, enterprise types, temporal validity, an APQC tree, local classification, unified search routing, and chunk-level semantic search.

At this point, the work separates vocabulary, relationship, time, classification, and retrieval so that a search result can retain a reason for being present. The immediate objective is to make the model explicit: what enters the system, what is recorded about it, and what remains outside the claim being made.

Why this matters

The implementation is deliberately layered: the architecture a model should make evidence more accountable, not hide uncertainty behind a single confident answer. This is why the work includes service contracts, stored records, and repeatable operations rather than a single broad description of “AI memory.” Each layer needs a job that can be inspected.

The implementation does not replace the judgment required to describe a business, a document set, or a working team. It provides a repeatable path for retaining the evidence that judgment uses. A technical decision is useful only when a later reader can see its scope, its constraints, and the result it was intended to support.

What I will test next

The next work will test this model in actual practice: whether the records can be retrieved at the right time, whether their provenance remains clear, and whether the system makes a real task easier without overstating what it knows. That distinction will guide the outcome posts that follow.

Historical basis: This entry is dated to the 2026-04-12 repository milestone, commits 6076ed0, 2b9ac0e, 4f2bf81, d94ae1b. It is based on the contemporaneous implementation records and their documented scope.
